title: Infinity mirror room
blurb: A raytraced 6-wall mirrored cube chamber in WebGL 2 that repeats one glowing floating HTML plaque across floor, ceiling and walls with green mirror-glass absorption per bounce, while projective updateElementGeometry() keeps the primary plaque editable and clickable.
question: Can a single raytraced 6-wall mirrored cube chamber repeat one glowing floating HTML plaque infinitely across floor, ceiling, and all four walls with physically authentic green mirror-glass absorption per bounce, while keeping the primary plaque interactive via projective updateElementGeometry()?
result: Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 (2026-11-27): all five live checks pass with zero console errors, 0.992 MP canvas at 412 px and DPR 2.625, real pointer clicks hit the Cyan palette, Ripple and input controls from front and back, and plain-HTML fallback activates when CanvasDrawElement is disabled. Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank are not verified yet.
